issues.failure_explanation: The approximate maximizer in (4.3-1) and the bound (4.4) are established with tolerance $(\Delta t)_m^{3/2}$, where $\Delta t=\max_i(t_i-t_{i-1})$. In the chain of inequalities this term becomes $\delta_m^{3/2}$ with $\delta_m=t_{k_m+1}-t_{k_m}\le(\Delta t)_m$, which is a smaller quantity, so the second inequality does not follow from (4.4). With the correct term, dividing by $\delta_m$ gives $(\Delta t)_m^{3/2}/\delta_m$, which need not tend to zero for non-uniform time grids (e.g. $\delta_m=(\Delta t)_m^2$), so the displayed $o(1)$ bound is not justified for the general grids allowed in the theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the near-maximizer in (4.3-1) with tolerance $(\min_k(t_{k+1}-t_k))^{3/2}$ (always possible since it is positive); then the tolerance divided by $\delta_m$ is at most $\delta_m^{1/2}\to0$ and the chain goes through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The sub/supersolution argument in the proof of Theorem 4.5 has an unjustified step for non-quasi-uniform time grids.
issues.title: Near-maximizer tolerance (Δt)_m^{3/2} silently replaced by δ_m^{3/2} in the subsolution chain
issues.why_classification: A one-line change of the tolerance in the choice of the approximate maximizer repairs the step with no loss of generality.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma asserts, with a constant $C$ independent of $h$ (and necessarily of the data $g$, since Lemma 4.9 applies it to the $h$-dependent data $F_{k+1}(v^h_{k+1})$), that $|D^\alpha I(g)|\le C\max_j|g(x^{(j)})|$ for $1\le|\alpha|_1\le3$. This is impossible for any interpolation scheme: take two collocation points $x^{(i)},x^{(j)}$ at the minimal distance $2\Delta_2x$ and data $g(x^{(i)})=1$, $g(x^{(j)})=-1$, $|g|\le1$ elsewhere on $\Gamma$. Since $I(g)$ interpolates and the segment between the points lies in the convex set $(-R,R)^d$, the mean value theorem gives $\sup_x|\nabla I(g)(x)|\ge 1/\Delta_2x$, while $\max_j|g(x^{(j)})|=1$. Under Assumption 4.3(i), $\Delta_2x\le\Delta_1x\to0$, so no $h$-independent $C$ exists. Hence Lemma 4.8 is false under its own hypotheses (or, if Assumption 4.3(ii) were unsatisfiable, Theorem 4.5 would be vacuous). The mechanism is a false stated result, not a proof step, so none of the three standard mechanisms applies exactly.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace Lemma 4.8 by a correct stability estimate (e.g. one with an explicit dependence on $\Delta_2 x$ or on regularity of the data) and rebuild the stability argument of Lemma 4.9 (likely requiring a CFL-type relation between $\Delta t$ and $\Delta_2x$) and hence the proof of Theorem 4.5.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4.9 (uniform $C^3$ bounds and time-Lipschitz bounds for $v^h$) is derived solely from Lemma 4.8 with $|\alpha|_1\le3$ and becomes unsupported; the proof of Theorem 4.5 uses Lemma 4.9 for finiteness of the relaxed limits, for (4.6), for the Lipschitz bound feeding $J_m\to0$, and for the hypothesis of Lemma 4.11, so the main convergence theorem is unproved. Lemma 4.10 uses only the $|\alpha|_1=0$ case, which is not contradicted but also not independently established.
issues.title: Stability Lemma 4.8 (derivative bounds by data maximum, uniform in h) is false
issues.why_classification: The central stability lemma is false as stated and the entire convergence proof rests on it; no comparable statement or repair is available in the source, and any fix requires new analysis and likely new hypotheses.

issues.failure_explanation: $\tilde u^\varepsilon=u^\varepsilon\zeta(\cdot/R)$ coincides with $u^\varepsilon$ only on $\{|x|\le R\}$. For $d\ge2$ the cube $(-R,R)^d$ (which contains $\Gamma$ and the points $x$ in the supremum) is not contained in this ball, so $I(\tilde u^\varepsilon)\ne I(u^\varepsilon)$ in general (data differ at collocation points with $|x^{(j)}|>R$) and $\tilde u^\varepsilon(x)\ne u^\varepsilon(x)$ for such $x$; the asserted equality fails.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma claims a $\delta_1$ valid for all $x\in\mathcal{O}$ and for $\varphi$ defined only on $\mathcal{O}$, but the expression $\varphi(x+\sqrt\delta w)$ with $|w|$ up to $\delta^{-\theta}$ requires $x+\sqrt\delta w\in\mathcal{O}$, which fails for $x$ within distance $\delta^{1/2-\theta}$ of $\partial\mathcal{O}$ for any fixed $\delta>0$.
